interest: This document provides an interesting operational perspective on U.S.-Japanese diplomatic relations in late 1939, illustrating how routine seasonal customs intersected with escalating geopolitical tensions. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's reports on the extended New Year holiday closures indicate that substantive diplomatic negotiations were effectively suspended, with only a skeleton staff present at the Japanese Foreign Office and cabinet ministers unreachable. In addition, as a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet, it offers archival value by revealing how the Foreign Service registered, summarized, and routed communications under decimal file 894.407.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.407, 'Social Matters., Japan, Holidays') consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet from late December 1939 tracking incoming diplomatic communications regarding holidays in Japan. It records telegrams from U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew informing the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE) about the upcoming New Year holiday period spanning January 1 through January 6, with government office closures commencing on December 29. The purports emphasize that while prevailing circumstances required a skeleton staff to remain on duty at the Japanese Foreign Office, official business requiring the consideration of cabinet ministers would be difficult or impossible to transact.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers docket sheet cataloguing incoming telegrams concerning Japanese New Year holidays and government office closures.
subfiles.summary: This document is a State Department 'List of Papers' index sheet for decimal file 894.407 recording communications regarding holidays in Japan in late December 1939. It summarizes telegrams dispatched by U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs detailing the closure of Japanese government offices from January 1 through January 6, starting as early as December 29. The recorded summaries note that although a skeleton staff would remain on duty at the Foreign Office due to current circumstances, official business requiring ministerial review would be virtually impossible to conduct.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Holidays in Japan
